# Perform Fligner-Killeen test for homogeneity of variances

<small>Source: [`man/performFlignerKilleenTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performFlignerKilleenTest.Rd) · Help: `?performFlignerKilleenTest`</small>

Non-parametric test based on ranks.

## Usage

```r
performFlignerKilleenTest(model, data = NULL, group)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   data frame used to fit `model`. When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used, so `group` must then be a variable of the model. The model frame holds the terms of the model rather than its variables (`log(x)` rather than `x`), so a model that transforms a variable needs `data`, as does a model with an `offset()` term.

`group`
:   name of the grouping variable.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the chi-squared statistic, p-value and degrees of freedom.

## Details

Absolute residuals are ranked after adjusting for group medians. The statistic approximates a chi-square distribution with \(k-1\) degrees of freedom.

## References

Fligner, M. A., & Killeen, T. J. (1976). Distribution-free two-sample tests for scale. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 71(353), 210–213.

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 mtcars$cyl <- factor(mtcars$cyl)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
 performFlignerKilleenTest(m, mtcars, "cyl")
```
